goal: Understand SQL window functions well enough to rewrite my self-join reports
interpretation: In 30 minutes of viewing across at most two videos, the learner understands window functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, ranking, frames, LAG/LEAD) well enough to replace their self-join based reports with window function queries in PostgreSQL.
assumptions: Self-join reports are typically things like previous-row comparisons, running totals, and top-N per group, which map to LAG/LEAD, window frames, and ROW_NUMBER/RANK.
Videos should use PostgreSQL or standard SQL syntax that works in PostgreSQL.
Two videos at most means the plan should favor one comprehensive practical video plus optionally one short complementary video, not many small ones.
No practice time is reserved, so the 30 minutes is all watching.

sub_topics.title: OVER() and PARTITION BY: window vs GROUP BY
sub_topics.why: The learner knows GROUP BY aggregates, so the key mental shift is keeping row-level detail while computing aggregates over partitions, which replaces self-joins to aggregated subqueries.

sub_topics.title: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK for top-N per group
sub_topics.why: Top-N per group and deduplication are common self-join/subquery report patterns that ranking functions replace directly.

sub_topics.title: LAG and LEAD for previous/next row comparisons
sub_topics.why: Comparing a row with its previous or next row is the classic self-join use case, and LAG/LEAD make it a single pass.

sub_topics.title: Running totals and window frames (ORDER BY, ROWS/RANGE BETWEEN)
sub_topics.why: Running totals and moving averages usually require painful self-joins with inequality conditions; frames replace them.

sub_topics.title: Rewriting self-join reports as window function queries
sub_topics.why: The goal is to convert existing reports, so seeing before/after examples of self-join to window function rewrites ties everything together.

picks.title: SQL Window Functions Explained: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD
picks.reason: A PostgreSQL walkthrough that goes from OVER and PARTITION BY through ROW_NUMBER/RANK/DENSE_RANK top-N per group, LAG/LEAD month-over-month growth, and running totals with ROWS BETWEEN. It is one practical video that covers most of the plan, so the learner has a single setup to follow. It also ends with common mistakes such as a missing ORDER BY inside OVER.

evidence.quote: A window function keeps every row and adds a calculated value next to each one.
Partition by decides which rows belong together. Order by decides the sequence inside each group.
LAG fetches the value from the row before, LEAD fetches the row after.

picks.confidence_note: Covers all four core sub-topics at the right level in PostgreSQL. Less sure because the segment map runs past the stated 15.5 minutes, so the real length may differ.

picks.title: SQL Running Total, LAG and LEAD, Moving Average, ROWS vs RANGE | Real-Time #6
picks.reason: A second pass through the report-style patterns a self-join normally handles: running totals restarting per partition, month-over-month change with LAG/LEAD, and moving averages with explicit frames. It also warns about the ROWS vs RANGE frame trap. These patterns map directly onto the learner's self-join reports.

evidence.quote: PARTITION BY customer. The running total restarts for every customer.
LAG reads the previous row's revenue, and LEAD reads the next row's.
ROWS BETWEEN TWO PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. That's this month plus the two before it.

picks.confidence_note: Strong on frames and LAG/LEAD in PostgreSQL. It never shows a self-join query side by side with its window rewrite, and its segment map also runs past the stated 7.6 minutes.
